content.text: A general question about documentation for the import-export tool ... Currently it appears as though there is documentation in two places: (1) the README.md for the project in github (
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export
) and (2) the Import and Export Tools page in the Administrator Guide on the Duraspace wiki (
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Import+and+Export+Tools

).  I'm not sure how these two documentation spaces related to each other.  It doesn't seem ideal to me to try to maintain detailed documentation in both places.  Do either of you have advice on how these two documentation spaces relate to each other and, in particular, where the documentation requested in this ticket should go?  Thanks.
: I would suggest trimming down the wiki documentation and creating a clear link to GitHub... where the complete set resides.
So, as a part of this task, please feel free to trim out some of the existing wiki docs:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Import+and+Export+Tools

I've been looking at this issue and trying to figure out what I can reasonably do in the context of the current sprint.  What I was thinking of starting with is documenting the structure of an export, with some examples.  That would be a start toward clarifying what an import package should look like, though I realize that's not the same as documenting precisely the rules to which an import package must adhere in order to be importable using the tool.  Would that (documenting the structure of an export, with examples) be helpful at all in terms of what you're asking for in this issue?

I think documenting the structure of the export would be helpful.  I'm thinking about the use case where someone is importing something that wasn't explicitly exported from Fedora though, and trying to make a package from scratch that can be imported. I think to do that it's important to include a reference to the LDP containment structure that is required, and to indicate that any resources in the import package which are described in that model will be ignored (that was my experience anyway).
PR submitted that addresses a part of this issue; namely, documentation regarding the format of exported data –
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/pull/89
Pending response to "code review" comments.
Updated PR in response to review comments.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/commit/5103ee168f1ed19c2eefa720b230fe99c800629c
I did some work on this, to the extent of documenting the format of an export, along with a few simple examples –
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/import-export-format.md
.  The examples show a simple LDP containment case if that's of any use to you.
I think that's very helpful. Thank you!

This task is to improve the import/export documentation to be more verbose about what it expects the contents of a directory to be imported to look like, and what model the resources needed to adhere to.  Or at least some pointers to existing documentation on that topic.
For example:
The Fedora 4 Import/Export Utility is designed to export data from, and import data to, Fedora 4 for uses such as:
Migrating or synchronizing data from one repository to another
Exporting data for backup or preservation
Note: The Import/Export Utility does not perform any data mapping or transformation — it can be used to import new data into Fedora, but the data would need to conform to Fedora's requirements.
..also include a link to where one can find the description of "Fedora's requirements"
